correctness.rationale: Every nonselected edge imposes exactly one chosen adjacent edge. At degree-two interiors this becomes a three-bit condition, and at each theta endpoint it depends only on the three first/last bits. The explicit four-state transfer matrix counts all bit sequences, with exact equality T^4=T^3+T verified by multiplication, giving F(a,b,c)=F(a-1,b,c)+F(a-3,b,c) whenever a>=6, and cyclic trace gives matching cycle recurrence. All twenty unordered triples with parameters 2..5 have nonnegative gap and exactly one zero; the standalone verifier independently exhausts original edge subsets in each case. Induction gives the nonnegative gap for all integer triples and uniqueness of equality at (2,2,2). Tests supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The fundamental bicyclic theta family consists of all subdivisions of K2,3. Establishing the open cycle extremal inequality for every such graph, with exact equality only at the unsubdivided K2,3, gives a meaningful infinite class beyond paths, trees and earlier unicyclic examples. The explicit four-state all-parameter count and common recurrence are reusable structural tools; no arbitrary cutoff, isolated table-only claim, or generic algorithm renaming is presented.
